messages:
sam taylor: hi everyone, first week here. triggered the onboarding pipeline but it fails on docker pull with a 403 and then checkout error. not sure what's wrong. any starter checks?

ira nguyen: welcome! can you paste the build link and the two error snippets (image pull + checkout)? are you running on k8s agents or EC2?

sam taylor: Build link: https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/builds/123
Image pull error:
```
ERROR: Denied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/buildkite-agent-role/i-0bb22 is not authorized to perform: ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability on resource: arn:aws:ecr:us-east-1:123456789012:repository/redwood/onboarding-base
```
Checkout error immediately after:
```
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood/my-service.git/': The requested URL returned error: 404
```

kevin zhao: two separate issues likely: 403 from ECR -> IAM/IRSA or missing imagePullSecret; 404 on checkout -> GitHub App/webhook or repo install problem. which agent type did you pick?

sam taylor: k8s agents (cluster bk-us-east). i accepted the GitHub App invite yesterday.

devops-bot: Tip: For EKS, pods either use imagePullSecrets (docker creds) or IRSA-mapped service accounts for ECR access. Local aws creds won't affect pods. For checkout 404, check that the GitHub App is installed on the target repo and that SSO hasn't blocked the app installation.

ira nguyen: ok first step (ops) — check if `buildkite-docker-creds` secret exists in `buildkite` namespace and whether the pipeline's helm values set that in `imagePullSecrets`. second (IRSA) — check the serviceAccount annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` mapping or the node IAM role has ecr:* permissions.

kevin zhao: for the 404 on checkout: GitHub returns 404 if the Buildkite GitHub App isn't installed on that repo or if the repo is private and the app token lacks access. Ask an org admin to verify the app installation and SSO approval. Also check Buildkite project settings -> repository access method (should be GitHub App).

sam taylor: i don't have cluster perms yet to view secrets and can't see org app installs.

ira nguyen: i'll grant you view in `buildkite` namespace and check infra. quick command ops uses to create secret: 
```
kubectl -n buildkite create secret generic buildkite-docker-creds --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=/tmp/dockerconfig.json --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
```
If the pipeline uses IRSA instead, we need to ensure `buildkite-agent-sa` is annotated and the IAM role has `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`, `ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability`, `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer`.

kevin zhao: infra, can you confirm the GH App install for `my-service`?

(ira checks and infra responds)

ira nguyen: granted sam view perms and recreated `buildkite-docker-creds` from the central CI key. infra also noticed the repo's GitHub App installation was in a pending state due to SSO approval — pinged org admins and reinstalled the app.

sam taylor: re-running the build now...

(30s later)

sam taylor: nice 004 success — image pulled and checkout worked. thanks for the quick help.

kevin zhao: i'll add two short onboarding checklist lines: 1) If image pull 403 -> check imagePullSecrets, then IRSA SA annotation, then IAM role ecr actions; 2) If checkout 404 -> check GitHub App install on repo, SSO approval, and Buildkite repo settings.

devops-bot: Note: local `aws ecr get-login-password` is useful for local testing but won't unblock pods. Use `kubectl describe pod` to inspect ImagePullBackOff events and `kubectl -n buildkite get secret` to verify secrets.

sam taylor: adding to my notes, super helpful. excited to get started!
